answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one willow trap before the comet window. It soaks the trap and files a pearl count with soak hours. An auditor recomputes the catch at four pearls per hour from the public soak table and checks its log; mismatch or reused logs burn the bond and void payment. First filing costs 33; the kth fake pays 33+5(k-1), the 1,000th pays 5,028, and 1,000 fakes cost 2,530,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trap ring fails: one key serves one identity, so duplicate logs burn both bonds. An honest identity pays 33 once and recovers the bond after audit.
